title: pydantic/monty — A minimal, secure Python interpreter written in Rust for use by AI
content:
Note
Hack Monty Round 3 is live - the last round before Monty V1. See pydantic.dev/monty for details.
Monty runs Python written by a model with no container, VM or sandboxing service in the loop. Creating a sandbox and running ten commands in it takes 5 ms (Docker: 900 ms, a sandboxing service: 1900 ms), a paused interpreter serialises to bytes you can resume later, and memory, time and recursion limits are enforced by the VM itself. Filesystem, environment variables and network do not exist inside the sandbox: it reaches the host only through the functions and mounts you pass in.
Documentation: pydantic.dev/docs/monty
uv add pydantic-monty        # Python
npm install @pydantic/monty  # JavaScript / TypeScript
cargo add monty              # Rust
The commercial Full Monty runs the same workers as a container image.
The code string is what a model writes when asked how long a bar of chocolate could power a lightbulb:
from pydantic_monty import Monty
code = """
kcal = nutrition('chocolate bar')['kcal']
hours = kcal * 4184 / (bulb_watts * 3600)
print(f'a chocolate bar powers a {bulb_watts} W bulb for {hours:.1f} hours')
"""
with Monty() as pool:
    with pool.checkout() as session:
        session.feed_run(
            code,
            inputs={'bulb_watts': 10},
            external_lookup={'nutrition': lambda food: {'kcal': 230}},
        )
        #> a chocolate bar powers a 10 W bulb for 26.7 hours
nutrition ran on the host and the sandbox saw only its return value.

report.summary: Pydantic releases Monty, a Rust-written minimal Python interpreter that runs AI-generated code in a 5ms in-process sandbox with no container or VM.
report.background: AI agents increasingly write and execute code as a tool call, but running model-authored Python safely has meant heavy machinery: Docker containers, Firecracker microVMs, or hosted sandbox services like E2B. These add hundreds of milliseconds to seconds of startup latency, which compounds badly inside multi-step agent loops, and they still expose a filesystem, environment and network unless carefully locked down. Meanwhile CPython's interpreter internals were never designed to be cheaply snapshotted or hard-limited per execution. Pydantic, known for its validation library and the Pydantic AI agent framework, built Monty to collapse that whole layer into a library: a purpose-built Python subset interpreter in Rust that enforces its own resource limits and reaches the host only through explicitly passed functions and mounts. It ships as part of Pydantic's production agent stack alongside Logfire observability and an LLM gateway.
key_points: Speed is the headline: creating a sandbox and running ten commands takes about 5 ms in Monty, versus roughly 900 ms for Docker and 1,900 ms for a sandboxing service. That difference matters because agents may execute dozens of small code snippets per task, and sandbox latency is pure overhead in every loop iteration.

The security model is subtractive rather than perimeter-based. Inside the sandbox there is no filesystem, no environment variables and no network at all. Code touches the host only through functions and mounts you explicitly pass in, as in the example where a nutrition() lookup runs on the host and the sandbox only receives the returned dictionary.

Resource limits — memory, time and recursion — are enforced by the VM itself rather than by an external cgroup or watchdog, and unlike in-memory sandboxes, a paused interpreter serialises to bytes so execution can be suspended and resumed later, enabling durable or human-in-the-loop agent workflows.

Monty implements a Python subset, not full CPython, so compatibility is deliberately bounded; it is distributed as a library via uv add pydantic-monty, npm install @pydantic/monty and cargo add monty, with a commercial 'Full Monty' container image for teams wanting the same workers in a container.

It is already wired into Pydantic AI as the Code Mode execution layer, supported by community bindings gomonty for Go and dart_monty for Dart and Flutter, and Pydantic is running Hack Monty Round 3 as the final competition before the Monty V1 release.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Monty reframes code execution as an embeddable library primitive rather than a piece of infrastructure, undercutting the value proposition of latency-heavy sandboxing services and pushing hosted sandbox vendors toward longer-running, heavier workloads. For agent developers, it removes a major source of friction: fast, deterministic, dependency-free sandboxing that works offline and serialises to bytes means agents can call code hundreds of times per task, resume mid-execution, and run in environments where Docker is unavailable or banned. For regular users, the practical effect is snappier, more reliable agents that can calculate and manipulate data instead of hallucinating results, with a smaller blast radius if the model writes something malicious, since no filesystem, network or secrets are reachable unless explicitly granted.
report.tools: Try Monty via pydantic-monty (Python), @pydantic/monty (JS/TS) or the monty crate (Rust), and follow the docs at pydantic.dev/docs/monty. If you build agents, pair it with Pydantic AI for Code Mode and Logfire for tracing. Worth comparing against E2B, Docker, Pyodide and WASI runtimes when choosing an execution layer, and watch gomonty and dart_monty for other language bindings, plus the commercial Full Monty image if you need container parity.
